claims: The Artemis II crew successfully landed on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Orion capsule arrived at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis II crew were recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
The landing type was parachute-assisted splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
The landing location was near San Diego, CA.
The landing time was April 10, 2026, 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The recovery ship was USS John P. Murtha.
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew completed a 10-day mission.
The Artemis II crew were the first humans to travel around the moon in over 50 years.
